observations.seen: The bike and astronaut read as near-uniform white-cyan with blown highlights and almost no form shading. There is no directional key from a low sun. Ambient fill dominates every frame, so the 'golden-hour' recipe is absent.
The bike shows only a faint purple smudge under it on the terracotta ground in frame 1. Rocks, posts and the track ribbon cast no visible shadows, so objects float with no grounding.
The white and teal fairing is fully matte, with no environment reflection of the nebula sky or the moon. The chrome-looking wheel hub has no specular response.

The stylized setting has a nebula skybox, a large pale moon, a beaded ribbon track on stilts, and floating low-poly boulders over a starfield void. It reads as a coherent concept. However, the ground plane is a smeared, blurry terracotta texture with no surface detail, and the world feels sparse.

Distant mountains and the track carry slight haze. There is no real depth fog falloff: mid and far boulders hold the same contrast. There is no dust, trails or particles behind the bike, despite the 'stardust' theme.
The bike reads as flat plastic. The ground texture is low-resolution and smeared. Rocks are flat-shaded facets with simple color variation. There is no roughness or metal differentiation anywhere.
The astronaut and sidecar bike are a reasonable hero asset. The rocks are basic icosphere chunks, and the poles and posts are plain tapered cylinders scattered without design intent.

In frame 2 the subject is centered at roughly 15% of the frame, which is acceptable. In frame 4 the countdown '3' overlaps the moon, and the HUD panels collide with the letterbox. In frame 2, the 'Leave a little stardust' text sits directly over the bike.
The chase framing at an FOV near 60 works in frame 2. In frame 3 the bike rolls and drifts low in frame during zero-G, losing a readable horizon.

Heavy soft bloom and haze wash out contrast across all frames. The letterbox bars in frame 4 crop the HUD itself: the position, lap and speed panels are cut off, and the speed digit is sliced. There is no film grade, vignette or warm tone curve.

The dark rounded HUD panels are clean and readable, showing position, lap, race time, standings, the stardust bar and speed. However, the center-screen tutorial text overlays the bike. The cinematic bars clip the panels during the countdown.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
